title: A one-line `/review-code <brief>` spawn silently drops the brief, and a reviewer that saw nothing can publish as completed with no findings
outcome: A spawn's brief always reaches the child or the spawn refuses, and a review that had nothing to review can't read as a clean review.
acceptance: A single-line command prompt with trailing text either carries the text to the child or refuses at spawn; it is never dropped silently, shown by a behaviour test for both Codex and Claude children.

The injected reviewer protocol distinguishes a completed review of a real change set with no findings from no supplied input or no change set, which must be reported as failed with a reason. A behaviour test shows that such a failed result is not published or displayed as a clean completed review. This relies on reviewer compliance: it does not machine-reject a contrary completed submission, and introduces no schema, legacy or persistence change.
A review pair has no Medium or higher and the normal gate passes.

completion.summary: Single-line template briefs are appended rather than silently lost, with both vendor spawn boundaries covered. No-input reviewer guidance requests failed-with-reason, and existing typed failure stays failed through contradictory prose, parent fan-in and persistence. Author71 and exact-tree composite full gate passed; no Medium+ remains. Landed in combo28 4c377a63. Cleanup of author root follows; review originals retained for open optional children.
